newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets Puerto Vallarta port for privatization.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets Puerto Vallarta port for privatization.

text.p: Mexico's Communications and Transport Ministry on Thursday announced the upcoming sale of a 25-year concession to operate Puerto Vallarta's port.
A full 100 percent of the assets of the Pacific coast port administration will be privatized, with just 49 percent available to foreign companies, the ministry said.

The privatization will be led by Banco Santander in Mexico with applications to submit bids due by July 31, the ministry said in the Official Gazette. A decision on the winning bidder is scheduled by Dec. 19.

This is the second time the ministry will set out to privatize Puerto Vallarta's administration. The sale was cancelled in December 1995, when sole bidder Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) won the concession for Acapulco's port and was disqualified from Puerto Vallarta.
Mexican privatization law prohibits any single company from operating two of the same type of port. Both Pacific resorts are both key tourism ports.

Puerto Vallarta is the second-largest tourism port in Mexico, with revenue of more than 1.5 million pesos in the first half of 1996. The cost of operating the port has been estimated at about 20 million pesos per year.
Mexico is in the process of privatizing the formerly government-run port administrations.
